I farm only 6 mu, so I will keep my plan simple, controlled, and aimed at stable output rather than chasing the absolute highest yield. Since I already have a wheat-maize rotation and access to well irrigation, I will continue with that system on all 6 mu. I have a university education and five years of farming experience, so I prefer improved seed, measured fertilizer use, and timely field operations instead of rough, traditional management. Because some family members work off-farm, I will avoid management that is too labor-intensive. For wheat, I will use improved seed, moderate-to-high nitrogen with balanced phosphorus and potassium, irrigate several times because winter wheat in Hebei depends heavily on water at key stages, and use rotary tillage because it fits my scale and saves labor. For summer maize, I will plant hybrid seed for stronger yield potential, apply a bit more nitrogen than wheat, keep phosphorus and potassium balanced, irrigate fewer times because the rainy season helps, and reduce tillage pressure by using rotary tillage again after wheat harvest so I can sow quickly. I will keep pesticide use limited but not zero, because protecting yield matters more than saving a small amount on chemicals when my land area is small.
